\(\text{(i) } (-6)^2 \quad \text{and} \quad \text{(ii) } -6^2\)
questions.solution:
Let's carefully distinguish the role of parentheses in indices:

  • Expression (i) \((-6)^2\): The exponent \(2\) applies to the entire quantity inside the brackets, including the negative sign:
    \((-6)^2 = (-6) \times (-6) = 36\)
  • Expression (ii) \(-6^2\): The exponent \(2\) applies only to the base number \(6\), and the negative sign is applied afterwards:
    \(-6^2 = -(6 \times 6) = -36\)

Therefore, (i) equals \(36\) and (ii) equals \(-36\).
